procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory before applying for a certificate. Registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added, and takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade operates the e-service 'Certificate of Origin for India'. The exporter logs in to the ministry e-services portal and chooses this service.
The exporter fills in the application form with the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product. Each item must qualify separately in its own right.
The exporter uploads proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
The exporter pays the certificate fee online. The fee is AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000 (band: AED 10 to AED 200).
The exporter submits the application and receives approval, or a return with comments to correct.
The exporter prints the approved certificate.
The competent authority issues the certificate before, at, or within five working days of export. It is valid for twelve months from issue and covers only one import.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and conducting a factory visit.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed. The importer keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing and must answer a customs request within ten working days.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.

The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD), and the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess only for lines in Table II. IGST, GST compensation cess and the Social Welfare Surcharge still apply, as do any anti-dumping, countervailing or safeguard duties. Because the IGST base includes BCD, a lower BCD also lowers the IGST amount.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Indian inputs count as originating only with proof of their originating status (bilateral cumulation, Art. 3.7).
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
The operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 (a) to (q), alone or combined, never make a product originating, whatever the product-specific rule says.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
Indirect materials (such as fuel, tools and consumables used in production) count as neither originating nor non-originating.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating. The last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.

Inference: a producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

Fee bands are those of the certificate service (UAE e-service: Certificate of Origin for India; Ministry service pages; Cabinet Resolution 208/2025 fee schedule), charged on the invoice value in AED. Assumes the certificate's invoice value equals the shipment value given.

Preference is given only to originating goods shipped directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar.
An invoice issued by a third party does not by itself cause the claim to be denied; the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.
